The general principles as to when a mere suit for permanent injunction will lie,
and when it is necessary to file a suit for declaration and/or possession with injunction as a consequential relief, are well settled.
We may refer to them briefly.
11.1) Where a plaintiff is in lawful or peaceful possession of a property and such possession is interfered or threatened by the defendant, a suit for an injunction simpliciter will lie.
A person has a right to protect his possession against any person who does not prove a better title by seeking a prohibitory injunction.
But a person in wrongful possession is not entitled to an injunction against the rightful owner.
11.2) Where the title of the plaintiff is not disputed, but he is not in possession, his remedy is to file a suit for possession and seek in addition, if necessary, an injunction.

A person out of possession, cannot seek the relief of injunction simpliciter, without claiming the relief of possession.
11.3)

Where the plaintiff is in possession, but his title to the property is in dispute, or under a cloud,
or where the defendant asserts title thereto and there is also a threat of dispossession from defendant, the plaintiff will have to sue for declaration of title and the consequential relief of injunction.

Where the title of plaintiff is under a cloud or in dispute and he is not in possession or not able to establish possession, necessarily the plaintiff will have to file a suit for declaration,
possession and injunction.
(Underlying by me, for emphases)
32. The notification produced by the plaintiff as well as defendants are clouded over the title of the plaintiff.
In such circumstances the plaintiff has to seek declaration of her title over the suit schedule property and also she has to prove her title by producing survey records not by revenue documents.
The revenue records produced by the plaintiff are stands in the name of original owner.
The plaintiff has produced tax paid receipts as per settled law.
Revenue records maintained by the state for collection of revenue.
Based on these documents the plaintiff has to seek for declaration of her title and possession over the suit schedule property.
By considering all these aspects, it is held that the plaintiff is utterly failed to prove her possession over the suit schedule property.
The defendants have acquired the land bearing Sy. No.40/1, 40/2, 40/3 as per law.
The said notifications are not at all set aside by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka or Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The defendants have acquired possession of the aforesaid land in accordance with law.
The plaintiff has filed this suit without challenging the notification issued by State Govt of Karnataka.
The simple suit for bare injunction is not maintainable.
Therefore it is held that, the plaintiff is utterly failed to prove her lawful possession over suit schedule properties.
Hence I answered issued No.1 in the Negative.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The plaintiff has filed this suit against the defendants for the relief of permanent injunction.
In the year 1992 Ramaiah was formed a private residential lay out thereon.
Said Ramaiah and his children were alienated the revenue site to certain persons through their registered instrument of power of attorney.
The plaintiff has purchased the schedule-I and II properties through registered sale deed on 06.10.2003 by paying sale consideration of Rs 3,000/-.
The plaintiff is paying revenue / tax of Govt or local authorities.
4. The State Government of Karnataka issued preliminary notification on 3.2.2003 for purpose of acquisition of land for formation of ARKAVATHI Layout.
Further issued final notification on 22.3.2004.
At that time Government has not been acquired land bearing No 40/P1P1 measuring 2 acres 16 Guntas.
The defendant No.1 to 5 have not right interest and title over said land and also no rights to disturb the lawful possession and enjoyment of suit schedule properties.
5. The defendants have highhandedly, illegally and without notice the defendants try to attempt dispossess the plaintiff from suit properties.
The plaintiff has resisted the illegal acts of defendants.
Therefore, they have no right to claim any interest over suit schedule properties.
In pursuant to order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the plaintiff has got issued legal notice to defendants as contemplated U/Sec 80 of CPC and U/Sec 64 of BDA Act.
On 10.09.2014 the defendants have attempted to interfere with peaceful possession and enjoyment of suit schedule properties of plaintiff.
No.40/P1P1 measuring 2 acres 16 Guntas and BDA has no authority, has no right, title, interest over the suit schedule property.
9.
The defendant BDA is the absolute owner of the suit schedule properties by virtue of acquisition as per notifications.
The defendant BDA is lawful possession of the property.
The defendant BDA is the absolute, separate exclusive, and acquired property.
Therefore the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable, it is barred by limitation and court fee paid by the plaintiff is not proper.
The BDA has taken possession of these lands by drawing Mahazar as per final notification and award.
Therefore plaintiff is not at all in possession of the suit schedule property.
Prior to filing of this suit, the plaintiff has got issued legal notice to the defendants as contemplated under Section 64 of BDA Act and 80 of C.P.C.
opennyai_summary.issue:
1. Whether the plaintiff proves that she is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit property as contended in the plaint?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendants are illegally interfering in the suit properties as shown in the plaint?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitle for permanent injunction as sought-for?
4. What decree or order?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the basis of said sale deed, Ramaiah was in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property till 1992.
In the year 1992, Ramaiah and his children were formed private residential layout in the said land.
They have sold the certain flats to different persons through GPA holder.
The defendant has taken contention that, as per the preliminary notification Ex.P61 and final notification as per Ex.P62, the Government of Karnataka acquired the land bearing Sy. No.40/1,
40/2 and 40/3.
It is clearly shows that the defendants without having any right, title over the suit schedule property they try to demolish the structure over the suit schedule property.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The plaintiff has proved her possession over the suit schedule property by relying on digital photos.
The plaintiff has successfully proved her case.
Hence prays for decreed the suit of the plaintiff and restrain the defendant by granting permanent injunction.
The acquisition made by the Government is in accordance with law.
The plaintiff is not at all in possession of the suit schedule property.
Therefore these documents are inadmissible as law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anvar V/s Basheer's case [(2014) 10 SCC 473] and Arjun Pandit Rao Khotar's case [(2020) 7 SCC 1].
